intended_object: The function ε ↦ ((√7/10)/500 · ε) / (1 − (c_high/500) · ε), where c_high = (1 + 1/√3)/2 is the upper Ritz coefficient. It is the exact, closed-form bound on the angle for the upper Ritz vector (eigenvector) in the worked numerical example of Davis–Kahan (1970), Section 9. I inferred this from the docstring, the module documentation, the matching lower-Ritz definition next to it, and how it is used in `final_upper_individual_angle_bound` and `NumericalExampleCertificate`.
explanation:
This defines one specific explicit real function tied to the paper's Section 9 example, so it cannot be too narrow, and Mathlib has no counterpart. It has the same shape as the library's other bounds in this file, a numerator coefficient times ε divided by 1 − (Ritz coefficient/500)·ε, where 500 is the spectral gap of the example. It reuses the √7/10 numerator of the lower-Ritz version and uses the upper Ritz coefficient in the denominator, as its docstring ("upper-Ritz-vector version") says.

The numbers agree with the printed decimal bound 0.00053ε/(1 − 0.0016ε) that the library proves above it: (√7/10)/500 ≈ 0.000529 < 53/100000, and c_high/500 ≈ 0.7887/500 ≈ 0.001577 < 1/625. Both comparisons are proved in `upperIndividualAngleExactBound_lt_printed`.

The usual junk value from division applies when the denominator vanishes, but the library only uses the bound for 0 < ε < 100, where the denominator is positive. I could not check the exact constant √7/10 against the paper's text. It is consistent with the printed decimals, and there is nothing to suggest it is wrong.
